[quote=montfleur;61731978][b]September 6, 2028: A miserable morning[/b]

The silence of the Collete house was the most dreadful thing that had come upon the place since the scandal had broken out amongst Thývenic society, staff had been sacked, nannies replaced, and the object of the scandal quietly removed from the house like an unwanted food item. Now, Iosep Collete sat in the early hours of the morning in his office, puffing slowly on his cigar with a glass of bourbon sitting on the desk, undrunk.

His wife and children had gone to his cousin's home for the weekend and were due to arrive back during the day, but his wife did not say. Of course, Iosep did not wish to know when the woman would be back, for she had taken to sighing and looking pale since the scandal broke. 

Thus, he sat at the desk, the papers of the day untouched, the bourbon lukewarm, and the sound of the remaining servants cleaning the house for the arrival of the lady of the house; they paid no attention to the master of the house, nor to his quarters, and as such, they had accumulated a mess of items. 

A knock sounded on the office door as the valet entered the room, an old, doddering man by the name of Viktor who had served the family for three generations and who Iosep had insisted should retire. 

Sir, the morning paper is here, began Viktor, stutteringly.

Send it to the cook, I do not wish gto see it, waved Iosep.

Viktor nodded, and noting that his master was still in his nightgown, made haste to the wardrobe that sat in the office, opening it to produce a clean pair of clothes and a semi-pressed shirt. It is a bit wrinkled, nodded Viktor, moving to hand his master the hangers behind the screen that sat in the room. 

Dressing himself crudely, Iosep stepped out from behind the screen and lit another cigar, When is the lady supposed to arrive? he asked.

Three this afternoon, replied Viktor, Oh, and a donor called, they are worried. 

Tell the donor not to be concerned; all correspondence should be forwarded to my lawyer, intoned Iosep.

Will you be having breakfast? asked Viktor.

No, only grits and some black coffeethe usual, replied Iosep, Eliza came back last night yes? 

Oh yes, she went straight up to her room, replied Viktor.

Is she out today? asked Iosep.

She went out with the nanny to the station, nodded Viktor.

Iosep nodded once more and then sat down, finally sipping the glass of bourbon, I shall have the business brought to me today, but first I must see my wife. 

She is of ill content, replied Viktor worriedly.

I do not care, we have not slept in the same room in three weeks, surely she must be consoled, replied Iosep.

But, the Lawyer began Viktor.

The Lawyer is not married to my wife, snapped Iosep, Now get gone with you, he waved his hand. 

Viktor bowed and made his way out of the office.

Iosep sighed and placed the bourbon glass down, moving to fetch a letter opener he peered at the blade, Oh were this blade in my heart! He thought, placing it down suddenly in horror, What wickedness! He cried aloud, burying his face in his hands.

After a few moments he recomposed himself and went to work on the papers and letters of the day, the majority were the usual, donors, business partners, advertisers, however, one letter was from his great aunt Vita Paolina, who firmly informed him in her writing that she was visiting to set the house in order. 

He checked the date of the arrival, it was that day, dread rose up in his chest as he leapt from his seat and ran out into the hall, Viktor! He called, rushing to find the valet who was in the hall with one of the servants, Why did you not tell me dame Paolina was coming?! he exclaimed.

Sir, I do not read your mail, replied Viktor calmly.

Oh but you didnt recognise the address? Now in my hour of despair, that horrid woman is arriving, on this day?! declared Iosep.

I believe your wife invited her, replied Viktor.

Oh! exclaimed Iosep, So she had decided to make me feel miserably also, 

Sir, I will handle Madame Paolina, please, your study awaits, motioned Viktor, pointing back towards the office. Iosep frowned and replied, I do not wish to see her, keep her out of my sight, he then turned on his heel and walked off to his office.
 
The rest of the day passed for Iosep as a feeling of dread sat upon his chest, he had retired to his study and had sat there unmoving save to use the water closet and to eat a meagre lunch.

He had fallen asleep upon his desk when the grandfather clock in the hall rang three and the sound of voices echoed down the hall, three female voices and the voices of the servants, his wife and two daughters were back, and allegedly, the madame Paolina.

He rose from his desk and moved to the door, opening it he walked into the foyer of the house and caught site of the aunt, a large woman of fine cloth, who gave him a stern look before heading up the stairs.

His heart ached within him as he watched his wife and two daughters disappear from view, why just last year they had gone to the beach together and had such fun.

With a sigh he made his way back into his office, he had changed his mind about seeing his wife.[/quote]
[b]September 7, 2028: The Aunt[/b]

There is much to be said about Madame Paolina, the most senior of the Paolinae family, she was a stout woman of wide proportions, seen by many as both a dame and a brute. Having been born in the age of the Nouveau Riche de Rosenmarkke, had granted her an air of independence which she used in a manner most liberal, and of which not one person dared to argue for.

Having been summoned by her niece-in-law following the infidelity scandal that had arisen with Iosep, she sought only to set the children right, though by her design she intended to wrest the poor wife and children away from Iosep, who she had disowned privately.

Moira dear, the humidity here is awful! Exclaimed Vita, I should wonder if one was really meant to live in such a region,

Moira Collete, a quiet and simpering woman merely nodded, her pale features aglow in the evening sunlight that poured through the windows of the upstairs sitting room, she had been crying, once again.

Where are the children? She asked, a question she had asked repeatedly throughout the evening.

They are with the nurse, although, I daresay they are getting old, why young Pietro is nearly fifteen! He should be at lacademie, replied Vita with a nod.

OhI wouldnt dare send him to such a severe place, he would perish, replied Moira.

Hardly my dear, many great officers have come from that place, 

Moira nodded, Well perhaps once this fiasco is over Ill look into it,

Money troubles my dear? Asked Vita, picking up what Moira had set down.

Oh heavens, I wouldnt dare say that!  lied Moira, shuddering at her lie.

Well, nevertheless, nevertheless, we shall set things to order, nodded Vita with resolve.

The door to the room opened suddenly with great energy as the eldest daughter Eliza ran into the room, her skirts flowing about her, she suddenly paused in the middle of the room realising her aunt was sitting there, curtsying politely she walked over to her mother, who smiled faintly.

Where have you been? Asked Moira.

I was out with the workers, replied Eliza.

The workers? Asked Vita, The farm workers? She harrumphed disapprovingly.

Yes, the grape harvest is almost ready, and wellI wanted to snatch some grapes! Replied Eliza.

Well did you bring me some? Asked Moira with a twinkle in her eye.

But of course! Laughed Eliza, opening her palm to reveal a bunch of grapes, And Aunt Vita can have some if she wishes!

Vita gave a firm no and merely said, How was the Fête with Anna?

It was enjoyable, the talk was a bit dry, all about politics and reunification, and there was a colonel there, an odd sort of man, began Eliza rambling.

Vita held up her hand, You are wandering dear, please, slow down, or Ill lose weight at this rate! She exclaimed with a cough.

You met a colonel? Asked Moira.

Yes, although I cannot remember his name, our conversation was brief, he offered me a ride home, 

Did you accept? Asked Vita.

Wellno, I mean a strange man asks you into his car at night, oh heavens, thats a death warrant waiting to be signed, replied Eliza.

She has a point Vita, even high society has dogs, sighed Moira as she remembered that her husband was one such animal.

What was his name? Asked Vita.

I do not recall, come to think of it, it was some sort of Montfleurois name, but frankly I could care less! Declared Eliza, Mama where is father?

Your father is in his study most likely, or with the lawyer in town, do remember dear we have a court date this week, replied Moira.

So Ill take Pietro and Madeline to the market on that day? 

Yes, I have no wish for those two to see the inside of a courthouse, and well, Madeline has to get ready for her coming out at Annas, 

Vita smiled, Moira, I was thinking perhaps Madeline would like to have her coming out party at the De Lorraines, 

Moira gave a startled look, The De Lorraines?! She exclaimed.

Yes, a suggestion by my daughter, Anna, she apparently met one of the nephews or some acquaintances of the president, replied Vita.

Well I am sure she would enjoy it, but, oh well she is so shy, and the people of that circle are usually so stiff, replied Moira.

Vita frowned, But they are the new people, and they are international! Which is the new way of things, 

Well Ill ask her about it, but nevertheless, I must go instruct the cook on dinner, Moira said, rising from her seat, Eliza please go check on Pietro, make sure hes done his arithmetic,

Eliza nodded and walked out of the room after hugging her aunt.
